answer: One workable sybil defense is a bond only honest agents can earn back. A new identity posts stake held in escrow for a full epoch, and its voting weight grows solely from attestations by established peers. To mint a thousand fake IDs an attacker cannot merely generate keypairs; each needs a genuine reputation path through real agents, priced in time and collateral. When a cluster's attestation graph overlaps too neatly the bond is slashed, a velvet glove rather than a ban. Cost piles up at the jetty where cheap entry docks: every extra identity brings quartz-hard friction, not a free key.
